name: Define DB, ORM, migrations, and id schema
description: Choose the database, data-access layer, migration engine, and primary-key convention before any persistence-backed feature. Document the choice in docs; do not add product tables.

acceptance.description: PRD records the chosen database, ORM/access layer, migration engine, and id convention.
acceptance.suggestions: Postgres. ORM: Drizzle + drizzle-kit scripts, or a thin pg controller without an ORM. Migrations: drizzle-kit or node-pg-migrate. IDs: UUIDv7 generated in app code before insert (no DB defaults on id columns).

acceptance.description: docs/architecture.md and docs/conventions.md describe the chosen layout and commands.
acceptance.suggestions: Keep persistence app-local under apps/web/lib/ until a second consumer appears.

acceptance.description: No product tables or business schema are added in this feature.

name: Local docker-compose for the chosen DB
description: Stand up a root docker-compose.yml service for the database chosen in feature 1 so local app work and future integration tests share one DATABASE_URL.

acceptance.description: docker compose up -d brings up the chosen database from the repo root.
acceptance.suggestions: Root docker-compose.yml Postgres service; template-generic credentials (not product-specific names).

acceptance.description: DATABASE_URL is documented for the app and future integration tests.
acceptance.suggestions: Document the URL in docs/conventions.md after the DB choice in feature 1.

name: Define backend API framework
description: Choose the HTTP API framework and write the composition-root / ports-and-adapters layout into architecture after the choice. No product routes.

acceptance.description: PRD records the chosen API framework and how it mounts into Next.js.
acceptance.suggestions: Elysia mounted in a thin Next.js catch-all app/api/[[...slugs]]/route.ts composition root.

acceptance.description: docs/architecture.md describes ports-and-adapters and factory injection for the chosen framework.
acceptance.suggestions: Route modules as factories; wire dependencies at the composition boundary; do not import process-wide service instances into route modules.

acceptance.description: No product routes are added in this feature.

name: EVM wallet login with SIWE
description: Arbitrum wallet login with better-auth SIWE, Postgres sessions, a protected home page, and sign out.

acceptance.description: Detected EIP-6963 wallets can connect and sign an Arbitrum SIWE message without a network switch; no-wallet and failure states are actionable.
Regular wallet signatures verify locally; only failed local verification falls back to Arbitrum RPC for smart wallets.
Successful login persists an anonymous session with app-generated UUIDv7 IDs; no email or ENS flow.
Logged-out requests to / redirect to /sign-in; logged-in requests show only the session user’s primary wallet address using a bounded query.
Sign out clears the session and returns to /sign-in, with pending and retryable error states.
Real Postgres integration tests cover sign-in, session, sign out, and wallet lookup isolation; lint, typecheck, build without env, tests, knip, and format pass.

review_notes: Login only. Contract calls and wallet views are deferred. Feature 3 remains pending; no API framework is selected.
